html:
The Chopcca are a Quechua-speaking people of the high Andes of Huancavelica in central Peru, a group of farming and herding villages that keep a strong identity of their own. They are known for their bright woven dress, their music and their festivals.

Their ancestors lived under the Inca Empire and spoke Quechua, the Inca state language. After the conquest the region became the home of the great mercury mine of Huancavelica, worked under the mita, the forced labour draft of the Viceroyalty of Peru. The mercury was used to refine silver at Potosí. Little else is written about the Chopcca as a separate group.
